item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J03095","case1_error":"Applies the 10% baseline at 65 inches instead of 66, adding three increments instead of two.","case2_error":"Subtracts the correctly calculated retained weight from the original, then triples the lost weight instead of the retained weight.","reason":"The first uses the wrong baseline; the second confuses a remaining quantity with its complement.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03096","case1_error":"Gives unsupported final numbers after correct deposit formulas, which yield $1,110.","case2_error":"Gives unsupported final number 280 after a correct earnings formula, which yields 221.","reason":"Both append incorrect final numbers to correct formulas without showing a numerical evaluation that explains those numbers.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J03097","case1_error":"Treats 15 training days per stage as 15 weeks, omitting division by five training days per week.","case2_error":"Compounds increases across days instead of using Monday's fixed baseline; also incorrectly evaluates 22.5 + 0.6 × 22.5 as 35.25.","reason":"The first fails to convert training days into weeks. The second changes the percentage baseline and makes an explicit arithmetic evaluation error.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03098","case1_error":"Performs four halving-and-donation rounds although the question specifies two.","case2_error":"Assumes walking for all 24 hours each day despite the stated one-hour daily walking duration.","reason":"The first adds extra process repetitions; the second substitutes elapsed calendar time for the specified daily activity duration.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03099","case1_error":"Uses the old $5,000 monthly salary for the new job, ignoring the 20% raise.","case2_error":"Represents '$1000 less' as adding $1,000 in the sale-price equation.","reason":"The first omits a required salary adjustment; the second reverses the direction of an explicitly stated subtraction.","judgment":"different"}]}
